from.place: Tag 0654 proof: a complex has Tor amplitude in [a,b] iff it has a bounded flat representative in [a,b]

title: Module Tor amplitude is equivalent to a bounded flat model
statement: Let A be a ring, let M^\bullet be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let a\le b be integers. The complex M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0 for every A-module N and every i\notin[a,b], if and only if there are a cochain complex P^\bullet of flat A-modules, with P^i=0 for i\notin[a,b], and an isomorphism M^\bullet\cong P^\bullet in D(A) [def-pc-derived-category].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.3 (Tag 0654; label more-algebra-lemma-tor-amplitude)

proof.text: For the forward implication, a complex P^\bullet of flat A-modules concentrated in [a,b] is K-flat by the bounded-above flat-complex theorem [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Therefore derived tensoring P^\bullet with any A-module N is represented by the ordinary tensor complex P^\bullet\otimes_A N, which is zero outside [a,b]; hence its cohomology vanishes outside [a,b].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.3 (Tag 0654), forward implication

proof.text: Conversely, assume M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. By the standard t-structure truncation description [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], replace M^\bullet by its canonical upper truncation at b; the map from this truncation to M^\bullet is a quasi-isomorphism because the cohomology above b vanishes, and the representative is zero above b. A bounded-above flat replacement of it, obtained by specializing [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to the one-point site of A, gives a quasi-isomorphic bounded-above flat complex P^\bullet vanishing above b. Since P^\bullet is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], its ordinary tensor with every A-module computes the derived tensor. Testing the Tor-amplitude hypothesis against every A-module N therefore shows that P^\bullet\otimes_A N is exact in degree a-1; the Tor criterion [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] makes the cokernel P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}) flat.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.3 (Tag 0654), converse implication and truncation

proof.text: Let E^\bullet be the complex with E^i=0 for i<a, E^a=P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}), E^i=P^i for i>a, with differentials induced by those of P^\bullet, and let P^\bullet\to E^\bullet be the evident surjection (this is the canonical truncation \tau_{\ge a}P^\bullet of Tag 0654). A direct computation gives H^i(E^\bullet)=H^i(P^\bullet) for i\ge a (in degree a both equal \ker d^a/\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}) and H^i(E^\bullet)=0 for i<a; since H^i(P^\bullet)=H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A)=0 for i<a by the Tor-amplitude hypothesis with N=A, the surjection is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its term E^a is flat by the Tor criterion [lem-pc-module-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] as shown in the preceding step, and E^i=P^i is flat for i>a. As P^\bullet is zero above b, E^\bullet is a complex of flat A-modules concentrated in [a,b] representing M^\bullet in D(A).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.3 (Tag 0654), truncation at degree a
